claims.sentence: Recent systems retrieve the cited work, locate candidate evidence and assign a verdict, typically including a partial-support category \citep{haan2025semanticcite,mocan2026refverifier,sadeghi2026deepsciverify,lee2026reflens,li2026bibagent}.
claims.claim: RefVerifier retrieves the cited work, locates candidate evidence and assigns a verdict that includes a partial-support category.
claims.excerpt: RefVerifier extracts citation-bearing sentences from manuscripts, checks bibliography metadata against scholarly databases, resolves references to full-text open-access PDFs, localizes relevant evidence passages, and generates verdicts with natural language explanations. ... Partially Supported: Evidence partially substantiates the claim but reveals minor overstatements, missing nuances, or scope shifts.

claims.sentence: Retrieval is incomplete: RefVerifier resolved 57.6\% of references in its test manuscripts to full text \citep{mocan2026refverifier}, and BibAgent infers support for paywalled sources from how other papers cite them rather than from the source itself \citep{li2026bibagent}.
claims.claim: RefVerifier resolved 57.6% of the references in its test manuscripts to full text.
claims.excerpt: We evaluated open-access PDF retrieval on 992 references cited across 23 randomly selected source papers from four research domains. RefVerifier resolves 57.6% (571/992) of these references to full-text PDFs.
claims.location: Sec. 4.1, Stage 2: Reference Retrieval Availability; Table 2 (p. 4)
claims.note: The 57.6% is right, but it was measured on 992 references from 23 randomly selected source papers, not on RefVerifier's test manuscripts (the end-to-end test set is a separate group of eight manuscripts, Table 6). The figure covers open-access PDF retrieval only, and the paper reports 93% title-match precision for downloaded PDFs, so not every resolved PDF was the cited work. Suggested rewording: 'RefVerifier resolved 57.6\% of 992 references, cited by 23 sampled papers, to open-access full text \citep{mocan2026refverifier}'.

claims.sentence: Locating the passage is harder in full text than in an abstract \citep{mocan2026refverifier,sadeghi2026deepsciverify}, and the full text is where many claims are supported.
claims.claim: Evidence localization is harder in full papers than in abstracts.
claims.excerpt: Localization performs better on SciFact abstracts, where the bi-encoder reaches a hit rate of 94%. Full-paper localization is more challenging.
claims.note: Supported as stated (deployed mode: 98% hit rate on abstracts vs 68% on full papers). Caveat: abstracts (SciFact) and full papers (Citation-Integrity) come from different datasets, so the comparison is confounded by dataset.
